title: Utility Standing Credit on Home-Site Lease Renewals
content:
A twelve-month renewal of the Home-Site Lease carries a utility-standing credit read from the Utility Pass-Through Service account serving the resident's site: a flat dollar amount per month, taken once from the monthly site rent written into the renewal.

**Desk rule.** With no utility late fee posted on that Utility Pass-Through Service account in the trailing 12 calendar months and a utility balance of zero or a credit, the credit is 2.00 per month. With no utility late fee in that window but a utility balance owing, it is 1.00 per month. Otherwise — a utility late fee posted in the window — there is no credit.

| Utility late fee in the trailing 12 calendar months | Utility balance on the account | Utility-standing credit |
|---|---|---|
| none | zero | 2.00 per month |
| none | a credit | 2.00 per month |
| none | an amount owing | 1.00 per month |
| one or more | any | none |

**Points of judgement**

- The account read is the Utility Pass-Through Service statement account serving the resident's site, not the rent ledger of the Home-Site Lease.
- A balance of exactly zero counts with a credit balance, on the 2.00 row.
- A utility late fee posted more than 12 calendar months before the signing falls outside the window and does not count.

*Hypothetical.* A utility account with no late fee in the past year and 38.12 owing on the current statement: 1.00 per month; a rent of 734.30 becomes 733.30.
